payload.question: Is the council collecting the rent its tenants owe?
payload.label: Council housing rent collected, excluding old arrears, Q1 2025/26
payload.council_caveat: The council's own explanation: "Cash collection in quarter one dropped compared to 2024/25, mainly due to the rise in Universal Credit (UC) claimants—now 55% of tenants. This shift reduced Housing Benefit payments by £1.5 million, with UC managed payments leaving a £110,000 gap… Rising living costs are worsening tenant finances." The council publishes these numbers as screenshots of a dashboard inside a PDF, so they cannot be read by machine. We read them off the images by eye, which is why this measure is flagged for human checking.
payload.evidence: Rent from council tenants pays for repairs, new homes and the debt on the existing ones, so a shortfall matters to every tenant. The council's own title for this indicator is "% of council housing rent collected (excluding arrears brought forward)", so unlike the council tax figure on this page it counts only the year's own rent. It aims to collect 99.8% and says it will step in below 98.8%. In the first quarter of 2025/26 it collected 96.88%.
